question: When two sessions or agents operate on the same working tree, does a broad staging operation sweep another agent's files, and do the advisory file leases actually prevent the overlap?
question_or_target: When two sessions or agents operate on the same working tree, does a broad staging operation sweep another agent's files, and do the advisory file leases actually prevent the overlap?
title: Concurrent-session races on the shared git index and file leases

reviewer.notes: Probe 2 re-derives the overlap from lease acquire + a conflicting write, not from probe 1's git diff --cached table.

method.probe1: Probe 1: run two agents against one scratch tree with overlapping file sets and inspect what each staging operation captured, using git diff --cached as the oracle.
method.probe2: Probe 2 (mechanically different): lease-level test - acquire a lease from one identity and attempt the conflicting write from another, recording whether the write is blocked, warned, or silently allowed; an advisory lease that nothing consults is documentation, not a control.

controls.note: harness isolation: scoped add of disjoint-a excludes disjoint-b
detector liveness: git add -A places agent-b/beta.txt in the index
tempfile scratch; live worktree is not GIT_DIR

tests.name: Overlapping agents with git diff --cached oracle
Disjoint file sets with scoped add must not interfere
Broad add must show a planted sibling in the cached set
All writes target a scratch tree, never the live worktree
Consult-fixture blocks non-holder and allows holder

targets.claim: A broad git add -A on one shared index stages another agent's files.
Two agents with disjoint file sets and a scoped add do not contaminate each other's index.
A file lease acquired by identity A prevents identity B from writing the leased path.
The shipped file-lease mechanism is consulted on write and is therefore a control, not documentation.

evidence.claim: Broad git add -A on a shared scratch index stages the second agent's files.
Scoped add of a disjoint file set does not stage the sibling, so the harness is not the contamination source.
A file lease held by identity A prevents identity B from writing the leased path.
The shipped file-lease mechanism is a consulted control.

findings.summary: Shared git index: git add -A sweeps a sibling agent's files. git diff --cached is the oracle.
No shipped file-lease API (IMP-0410 absent). A paper lease is documentation; the conflicting write is silently allowed.

residual_unknowns: Catalog reviewer_requirement asks for two different-vendor human reproductions; G-1 uses probe 2 as the independent instrument.
IMP-0410 specifies leases as advisory (log, never block); even a faithful implementation would not prevent overlap.

manifest_registration.note: per-unit only; global unit_manifest.py --write was not invoked

answer: CONFIRMED on the shared-index axis: a broad add on one scratch index stages the sibling agent's files (git diff --cached). REFUTED that file leases prevent the overlap: no shipped file-lease API exists, so a conflicting write is silently allowed; a consult-fixture both-states control shows what a real control would look like. Disjoint scoped-add isolation holds, so the harness is not the source of contamination. All writes were in tempfile scratch, never the live worktree.
